html:
The Bosporan Kingdom was a Greek kingdom on the Strait of Kerch, joining eastern Crimea and the Taman Peninsula, with its capital at Panticapaeum, now Kerch. It lasted from about 480 BCE into the 300s CE. The map shows it from 323 to 100 BCE; this page covers its Greek centuries, and the Bosporian Kingdom page its Roman ones.

It began as a league of Greek colonies founded by Miletus and other cities on the shores of the strait. From 438 BCE the Spartocid dynasty ruled for more than three centuries. The Spartocids called themselves archons to their Greek subjects and kings to the Scythian, Sindian and Maeotian peoples they also ruled.

Its wealth was grain. Wheat from the steppe, along with salt fish and slaves, was shipped across the Black Sea, and in the 300s BCE the kingdom was one of the main suppliers of Athens, which honoured its kings. The gold from its burial mounds, mixing Greek and steppe styles, fills museums today.

Under pressure from the Sarmatians and the Scythians, the last Spartocid handed his kingdom around 108 BCE to Mithridates VI of Pontus. After Mithridates' wars with Rome ended in 63 BCE, the kingdom passed into the orbit of the Roman Republic.
